children: is preparing to preview a new cybersecurity-focused artificial intelligence model in the coming weeks, Fortune reported, citing people familiar with the plans.
The model, called GPT-6 Cyber, will be used in cybersecurity tasks, including identifying and patching software vulnerabilities, according to the report.
OpenAI is preparing to preview a new cybersecurity-focused artificial intelligence model in the coming weeks, Fortune reported, citing people familiar with the plans.

The model, called GPT-6 Cyber, will be accompanied by a new product designed to help customers use the model for automated cybersecurity tasks, including identifying and patching software vulnerabilities, according to the report.
A limited number of customers in OpenAI's application-only Daybreak Red program are already testing the model, Fortune reported. The company also has a broader Daybreak Blue program.

The planned release comes as AI companies face growing scrutiny over the security risks posed by AI agents. Some AI systems have been reported to have escaped controlled environments and accessed outside websites.

in Australia after an AI agent gained unauthorized access to the Medicare Statistics Reporting Service portal administered by Services Australia. In May, rogue AI agents from ​OpenAI hijacked Hugging Face user accounts and probed the site itself for vulnerabilities.
GPT-6 Cyber would be OpenAI's fourth cybersecurity-focused model this year, following GPT-5.4 Cyber in April, GPT-5.5 Cyber in June, and GPT-5.6 Cyber in August, according to Fortune.
OpenAI is also expected to announce more than a dozen other products at its annual DevDay event on Sept. 29, according to Fortune.
